Nobody used the TEST-SET STRUCTURE: how the videos are cut from their recordings. Nobody read the dorado/Ultrack material as a validation source; it had only been used to train DaughterNet. I measured six gaps on the laptop (nice 19, scratch scripts border.py, overlap*.py, lfshift.py, pervideo.py, sixbba*.py, calib.py, ultrack*.py, attract*.py, contract.py; notes in research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_critic.notes.md).

(1) Overlapping crops. 44b6 is 71 overlapping space-time crops of one recording. 65 video pairs share GT at one (dt,dz,dy,dx) offset: dt up to +-91 frames, dy/dx 50-220 px, all mod-4 phases. 22% of 44b6 GT edge instances fall in multi-copy regions, and so do 25% of its FN (247/985, exp39+ef). Of those edges, 198 unique GT edges are DISCORDANT (TP in one copy, FN in the other); only 24 are FN in every copy. This is the only untouched source of GT-free evidence we have (hypothesis 1). 6bba crops are different: they share one acquisition clock (1,089 freeze-aligned pairs), but none of 645 time-aligned pairs overlaps in space. Phase correlation finds the known 44b6 overlaps at the exact offset (one pair is bit-identical on the overlap). So a hidden embryo is either overlap-rich (44b6-type) or has only the 1-frame time chaining (6bba-type; its clip-boundary ceiling is +0.0011, not proposed).

(2) Our lab is in-sample and the LB cannot resolve <0.002. Dorado regions outside the 44b6 clip boxes are out-of-sample images with dense Ultrack tracks. Those tracks agree with the human GT to a median 1.29 um (97% within 7 um), so they can serve as an out-of-sample judge (hypothesis 2).

(3) Error class nobody split by: the loss is a DENSITY problem. In 6bba, the densest quartile of videos (median 316 nodes/frame) holds 52% of the weighted loss (J 0.82, against 0.97 in the sparsest quartile); Spearman(J, nodes/frame) = -0.66. In 44b6 the densest quartile holds 38%. In dense videos the FN are 37% swap and 29% a_never. Every gate should report density quartiles, and the density of the test embryo decides transfer.

(4) Ultrack shows that in 44b6 the a_never FN are mostly UNDER-SEGMENTATION. Ultrack has a point 2.3 um (median) from the GT node, while our nearest node sits 1.9 um from a different Ultrack point about 7 um away. Ultrack also has ~44% more interior points than we do. A split/second-object head supervised by Ultrack is conceivable but not proposed: 91% of a_never FN are in 6bba, which has no Ultrack data, and added nodes pay the multiplier.

Measured dead ends (do not re-propose):
- A linefit displacement cap does nothing. a_linefit nodes are already 6.6 um from GT before linefit, linefit moves them 1.33 um, and only 13 of 226 move more than 3 um.
- Neighbour-repulsion correction. Annotated neighbour pairs 6-9 um apart come out 0.5-1.0 um farther apart in our output, mostly in z. But a GT-free contraction changes the <4 um share by <=0.0003.
- Spatial crop border. The FN rate is 6.5% within 2 um of the border against 4.2% in the interior. The clean excess is ~160 FN, a ceiling of +0.0012; the rest is confounded.
- Snapping to Ultrack points lowers the median distance but loses <4 um matches.

The division term has nothing new beyond B35/DaughterNet-B. The official window already accepts forks one frame late or early.

hypotheses.mechanism: The test videos are processed one at a time, but the only train embryo whose layout we can check for spatial overlap (44b6) is made of overlapping space-time crops of one recording. Its 65 overlapping video pairs have offsets up to +-91 frames and 50-220 px, with every xy phase mod 4. So the same nucleus is tracked 2+ times with different crop context: spatial border distance, clip-end distance and stride-4 sampling phase. On exp39+ef, 4,374 of 19,826 44b6 GT edge instances (22%) and 247 of 985 44b6 FN (25%) lie in multi-copy regions. Of those edges, 198 unique GT edges are DISCORDANT: FN in one copy, TP in the other. Only 24 are FN in every copy. The discordant FN cover every class: swap 49, a_never 46, a_tail 35, v_taken 28, u_diverted 24, linefit 9. The failing copy is the one nearer its crop edge: mean distance 9.7 um from its spatial border, against 14.4 um for the TP copy. The GT-free score min(spatial border um, frames to clip end) picks the correct copy in 70-71% of discordant cases (4% ties). Position averaging of agreeing copies adds a small de-quantisation gain: copies differ by a median 0.99 um, and the median GT distance falls from 1.34 to 1.24 um. Raw crops are bit-identical on the overlap (one checked pair has voxel equality 1.0), so a verified registration has zero false positives.
hypotheses.change:
Add a test-set pass after every video has its final graph (post-tail, after divinsert/float coordinates).
(1) Registration, GT-free. During detection, store per-frame z-MIPs (float16, 256x256). For every video pair, run batched GPU FFT phase correlation over dt in [-99,99]. Validate on the MIPs above the 6bba null. Candidate offsets need a peak > 0.06 that is not at (0,0), since (0,0) peaks are a fixed-pattern artefact. Then search dz. Accept a pair only if >= 99% of raw voxels on the 3D overlap are exactly equal.
(2) Correspondence. Map B's final nodes into A (t+dt, zyx+offset). Pair nodes by mutual nearest neighbour within 2.5 um in the overlap.
(3) Ownership. Each overlap location belongs to the copy with the larger min(spatial border distance in um, 1 um x frames to clip end).
(4) Fusion inside A, only in B-owned locations.
  (a) For a corresponded node whose successor differs between the copies, replace A's out-edge with B's out-edge mapped through the correspondence. This covers swap, u_diverted and v_taken.
  (b) A track end/start pair that B links becomes a link (break).
  (c) A short track deleted by A's short-track filter is kept when its B counterpart is a long track (a_tail). This needs the pre-filter graph.
  (d) A B node with no A counterpart is imported with its edges only if it links to corresponded nodes at both ends (a_never). Cap: +0.5% nodes per video.
  (e) Optional: average the positions of corresponded nodes.
  Forks are never touched, and nothing changes outside verified overlaps. On a 6bba-type test embryo the pass is an exact no-op.
hypotheses.upper_bound: 44b6-type embryo, per-embryo units (D_44b6 = TP+FP+FN ~ 21,148): fixing every discordant FN (~197 FN instances) gives +197/21,148 = +0.0093. If the FP edges of the failing copy flip too, up to ~+0.013. Pooled over the 199-video lab that is only +0.0015, because 44b6 is 15% of D. With the measured chooser (71% right, 25% wrong, 4% ties), the net is 0.46 x 198 ~ 91 FN-units = +0.0043 per 44b6-type embryo before seam losses. 6bba-type embryo: 0 by construction. Plus <= +0.0005 from position averaging (-7% median distance on only 22% of nodes).
hypotheses.expected_gain: Conditional on a 44b6-type embryo: +0.002..+0.004 on that embryo. The lab measures in-sample copies, where both are near-perfect, so test discordance and headroom are probably larger. The unconditional public expectation is about +0.001..+0.002, taking P(public embryo is overlap-rich) ~0.5 from 1 of 2 train embryos. Same for private. Costs: ~1 day of CPU engineering, <5 min extra runtime in the kernel (batched FFT on the GPU plus the voxel check), and 1 probe that doubles as a structure diagnostic.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low for harm, uncertain for size. (i) If the hidden embryos are tiled like 6bba, the pass never fires: zero gain, zero loss. (ii) Exact-voxel verification prevents fusing unrelated videos. (iii) The chooser is purely geometric (border and clip-end distance) and trusts no network output, so it avoids the in-sample-ILP trap that sank probe 30. (iv) The residual risk is seam artefacts from graph surgery. Bound them with the node cap, by leaving forks untouched and by allowing only edge replacement between corresponded nodes. (v) Policy: this uses only the hidden test images jointly. It never matches test clips against public recordings (the CONTEXT L3 policy).
hypotheses.not_closed_because: No closed or round-1 line uses information across test videos. It is not TTA: no extra views are computed, because the crops themselves provide the second view. It is not clustering or duplicate collapse (B31 / refined-duplicate-collapse), which merge within one video. It is not a relink knob, ILP trust or the edge filter. Clip-boundary and hole-fill were refuted because they lacked evidence; here the evidence is another crop's interior detection of the same nucleus, bit-identical input at different context. The 44b6 overlap was noticed only as a fold-leakage problem (make_splits), never as a signal.

hypotheses.mechanism: The lab is in-sample: the detector and edge network were trained on all 199 videos. That is why its ILP-trusting gains fail on the LB (ef_a0: SELECTION +0.0095, public -0.001). The public LB cannot resolve the items now waiting for a verdict: stitch +0.0021, float coords +0.0018, frozen ILP-first +0.0013, safe-div fork-midpoint +0.0007, overlap consensus, and the node-multiplier share of coordhead. The LB shows 3 decimals and moves about +-0.002-0.003 between identical submissions. There is a free out-of-sample judge. The public Ultrack dorado movie (522 frames, ~22.6k cells/frame) is the 44b6 recording, but only 39% of its samples fall inside the 44b6 clip boxes (register_44b6_dorado.py). The rest are images neither network has seen. Its dense Ultrack tracks follow the annotation convention: on the 63 placed 44b6 clips, GT to nearest Ultrack point is a median 1.29 um (91.7% < 4 um, 97.2% < 7 um), and our final nodes sit 1.46 um from Ultrack with no z bias. Ultrack also has ~44% more points than our nodes and noisy divisions (4.5x the GT rate). So it can judge continuation edges and positions, and it must be sparsified like the real annotation.
hypotheses.change:
Methodology plus one small GPU job; nothing ships by itself.
(1) In dorado coordinates, pick 24-32 boxes of 64x256x256x100 whose space-time footprints do not intersect any 44b6 clip footprint. Also keep away from where the 8 unplaced clips could be. Spread them over density quartiles.
(2) A private Kaggle GPU kernel (internet ON; allowed for non-submission runs), or Colab plus a dataset upload, streams the boxes from public.czbiohub.org/royerlab/ultrack/zebrafish_embryo.ome.zarr. It runs exp48 and exp51 end to end and writes friend-A-format caches (raw ILP geff, ckpt, dc, divnet) plus final graphs with float coordinates.
(3) Pseudo-GT geff per box, from Ultrack tracklets inside the box:
  - sample whole lineages covering 1% (44b6-like) and 10% (6bba-like) of points;
  - use only tracklets >= 20 frames with no Ultrack division, so the evaluation is edge-only;
  - set estimated_number_of_nodes to the Ultrack point count.
(4) Calibration on the 63 placed in-sample 44b6 clips: build the same pseudo-GT there and require that per-config deltas (exp39, ef_a0, ef_a3_rl_pr, st_all, lp030, float coords) have the same sign and a rank correlation >= 0.7 against real GT.
(5) Out-of-sample verdicts: the replay lab on the dorado boxes decides every sub-LB-resolution item and the finals bundle.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Indirect, decision value only. The items waiting for a verdict total about +0.006 locally (stitch 0.0021 + float 0.0018 + frozen 0.0013 + fork-midpoint 0.0007), plus overlap consensus (0-0.004 per 44b6-type embryo) and the coordhead multiplier question (~37% of x138's +0.007 may be node count). With 30 boxes x ~3,900 pseudo-GT edges (10% of ~390 Ultrack points/frame x 99 edges), the lab has ~117k evaluable edges, close to the real 129k. That resolves deltas of ~+-0.0005 (90% CI), against +-0.002-0.003 on one LB probe.
hypotheses.lab_test: Calibration first (CPU, no GPU, using existing tails and data_external/dorado/tracks/tracks.npz): the pseudo-GT and real-GT deltas on the 63 placed clips must agree in sign for all six configs. Kill the line if they disagree on two or more. Then the OOS run (about 1 GPU-h on 2xT4 for 30 boxes at ~2.5 min/video/T4, plus streaming). Success = it reproduces the known transfer failure: ef_a0 is at most +0.002 OOS (LB -0.001), while the in-sample lab says +0.0095. If that holds, the OOS lab becomes the gate for stitch, float, fork-midpoint, overlap consensus and finals composition. Report deltas per density quartile and the J-vs-multiplier split.
hypotheses.expected_gain: 0 direct. Expected +0.001..+0.003 on PRIVATE from decisions it enables: not shipping an in-sample artefact (probe-30 type, -0.001..-0.002 each), and shipping 2-3 real sub-resolution gains in the final bundle with evidence instead of hope. Cost: ~1 GPU-h, ~1 day of glue code (streaming, cache writer and pseudo-GT builder; the tools exist in register_44b6_dorado.py and dorado_crops.py) and 0 probes.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium, and it is a validation risk, not a submission risk. (i) Dorado is the 44b6 EMBRYO, so only the images and cells are unseen. Embryo-level shift toward the hidden test embryos is not captured, and 6bba-like conditions (freezes, high density) are under-represented. (ii) Ultrack pseudo-GT noise: 8% of GT nodes are > 4 um from Ultrack, and Ultrack over-counts by ~44%. Sparse sampling of long tracklets and the calibration step control this. (iii) Pseudo-GT sampling density changes which edges are evaluable, so run both the 1% and the 10% arms. (iv) Stay within policy: use only boxes outside every 44b6 footprint, and never touch hidden test data.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed item 'dorado pseudo-labels' (L3) TRAINED DaughterNet on Ultrack divisions, which proved too noisy (val AUC 0.62). This never trains on dorado. It uses Ultrack continuation tracks, which agree with GT to a median 1.29 um, as an out-of-sample JUDGE for edges and positions, on boxes outside the 44b6 footprints, so it also avoids the L3 leakage. The OOF-edge-scorer idea tried to fix the in-sample lab by retraining networks (refuted on cost and feasibility). This fixes it with unseen data and existing weights.
